<meta>continues from previous page: Therefore, three circles of the width of feet shall be made</meta> nine, and they should be distant from one another by one palm <gloss>a measurement of approximately four inches</gloss>; and in the middle circle, write first the name of the hour in which you perform the work; in the second place, the name of the Angel of the hour; thirdly, the seal of the Angel of the hour; fourthly, the name of the Angel who presides over 그 day on which you perform the work, and his ministers; fifthly, the name of the present season <note>Latin "tempus" in this ritual context refers to one of the four seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, or Winter, which change the names used in the rite</note>; sixthly, the name of the Spirits ruling in that part of the year and presiding over it; seventhly, the name of the head of the zodiacal sign ruling in that part of the year in which you perform the work; eighthly, the name of the Earth <note>referring to the specific magical name assigned to the Earth for that season</note>, according to that part of the year in which you perform the work; ninthly, and to complete the middle circle, write the names of the Sun and Moon, according to the aforementioned calculation of the season. For when the season changes, the names also change.

In the upper circle <note>the outermost ring of the diagram</note>, let there be assigned in the four corners the names of the angels presiding over the air on that day when you perform the work: namely, of the King and his three ministers. Outside the circle, in the four corners, let there be pentagons <note>five-pointed stars or figures used for protection</note>. In the lower circle <note>the innermost ring of the diagram</note>, let four Divine names be written, with crosses placed between them.
